December 8

2 (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.) (2 Corinthians 6:2 KJV)

The first part of this verse is a quotation from Isaiah (Isaiah 49:8). The point that Paul is making is that we need to know that now is the time to get saved, as Jesus told us that one can not come to Him, except he be drawn by the Father (John 6:44). So when a person hears the Gospel, and the Holy Spirit offers him salvation, you need to take it right then, as what if the Holy Spirit doesn’t ever try to draw you again. We need to make our commitment to Jesus when it is offered, as who wants to go to hell? There will come a day when the Holy Spirit will cease trying to draw people to the Lord (Revelation 22:11), and when that happens, all will then perish. Why take a chance of missing so great a salvation – you need to act while you have a chance. Many have mistakenly thought that they would have to give up to much, when they become a Christian, but that is not so. God gives you the desires of your heart, by putting His desires in your heart, and you will never be happier.

There are many people who have thought they would just wait until their last days to make a commitment to Jesus and be saved. But the trouble with that is, that as you live in sin, and let the devil have control of you, your heart becomes hardened toward God, and you will not ever reach the place of believing in Jesus for salvation, even if the Holy Spirit keeps asking you. So, if you hear the Gospel of Jesus Christ, and feel the tug on your heart from the Holy Spirit, you had better take advantage of it, and get saved. Your future in eternity is too important to be put off (Matthew 16:26), and possibly missed altogether. Come and join us Christians and live for God, and reap all the benefits that He offers His children. You must accept Jesus as your Lord and Savior, and be born again (John 3:3), by having His spirit come into you (Galatians 4:6), before you can be a Christian. Only by doing so, can you have the joy and peace that comes with Salvation, and nothing compares with that – Thank you Jesus for saving us!
